title: Historic Hotel Alex Johnson nominated for 'Best Haunted Hotel' in national contest
excerpt: Rapid City's historic Hotel Alex Johnson has been nominated for USA TODAY's Best Haunted Hotel. Learn how to vote daily through Sept. 21.
content:
RAPID CITY, S.D. (KOTA) - One of South Dakota’s most historic—and reputedly haunted—landmarks is in the running for a major national honor, and local supporters have a chance to help it claim the top spot.

The Hotel Alex Johnson, located in downtown Rapid City, has been nominated in the USA TODAY 10 Best Readers’ Choice Awards for “Best Haunted Hotel.”

The towering Tudor-style landmark has been a cornerstone of downtown Rapid City since the late 1920s, welcoming celebrities, dignitaries, and even U.S. presidents. Now, as the property approaches its 100th anniversary, General Manager Mitch McKeithen reflects on the unique legacy that has developed over the past century.

“Alex Johnson was a building started in 1927, alongside of Gutzon Borglum with Mount Rushmore. It was finished in 1928, which is when we opened the doors,” McKeithen said. “We’re coming up on our 100th birthday here in a couple of years. But yeah, there’s been a lot going on in the last hundred years.”

Part of that century-old history includes legendary ghost stories. The hotel actively leans into its spooky reputation, even keeping a guestbook at the front desk for visitors to document their paranormal experiences.

“All friendly things, from what I’ve seen. We have friendly ghosts here, nothing harmful,” McKeithen explained. “So it’s been fun. We have a ghost package you can purchase with the famous haunted Room 812, and you can get a K-2 meter to go ghost-hunting.”

While the spooky reputation is a popular draw, McKeithen emphasizes that preserving the hotel’s legacy requires balancing paranormal lore with world-class service. He hopes visitors recognize the historic landmark for both its friendly spirits and its high standards of hospitality.

“Being featured in a national contest as the best haunted hotel in America would be awesome,” McKeithen said. “Of course, I’d love to be known for our five-star hospitality that we give here over being just a haunted hotel. We have so much more to offer, but it’s a really cool draw, and it’d be really great exposure. Hopefully, you’re all proud of the Alex Johnson being an icon in Rapid City.”

Voting is open once per day through Monday, Sept. 21. To cast your daily ballot and support the historic landmark, visit the USA TODAY ’10 Best’ Voting Page
